This 2018 Subaru Outback 2.5i Limited Crossover is presented as a practical wagon-style vehicle with equipment aimed at everyday use. It has the Limited trim level, which places it toward the better-appointed end of the model range, and it carries the 2.5i designation for the 2.5-liter four-cylinder engine. The body shape provides the familiar Outback profile with a raised ride height and a long roofline, along with the space and versatility associated with the model. Subaru's symmetrical all-wheel drive is standard on this vehicle, and the Outback nameplate has long been associated with a combination of on-road comfort and light-duty utility. This example is described with the features listed below, and the cabin and exterior equipment reflect that focus on convenience and everyday usability rather than ornament.

Inside, this vehicle includes leather seats, which give the interior a more finished appearance than cloth upholstery alone. The seating surfaces are paired with a cabin design that favors straightforward controls and a driver-oriented instrument layout. The Limited trim also brings a more refined environment than the base versions of the Outback, with materials and trim details that fit the higher-grade specification. Subaru designed this generation of Outback with a roomy passenger compartment, and the extended body shape allows for a useful rear seat area as well as cargo space behind it. The seating position is elevated compared with a conventional sedan, and the large door openings make entry and exit straightforward. This interior arrangement is consistent with the Outback's role as a midsize crossover wagon, and the leather trim adds a distinct material treatment without changing the vehicle's basic function.

Technology equipment in this Outback includes premium audio, Apple CarPlay, and Android Auto. Those items place this vehicle in line with later-model infotainment expectations for 2018, and they provide a more current interface than earlier Subaru systems. The audio system is integrated into the center stack, where the touchscreen controls and related menus are arranged for direct access. Apple CarPlay and Android Auto add smartphone compatibility, and the factory system supports those platforms without requiring aftermarket hardware. The included technology also reflects Subaru's approach of combining a practical cabin with connected features that are easy to use during routine travel. This 2018 model does not rely on complex or unnecessary controls to provide its core functions, and the listed electronics fit that approach.

This Outback also includes a sunroof and a hands-free liftgate, both of which add convenience without altering the vehicle's underlying capability. The sunroof brings a glass opening to the roof area, while the power-operated liftgate allows rear access without using a manual release at the cargo door. Those features are part of the equipment set on this Limited trim and are commonly paired with the model's more upscale content. Outside, the Outback's shape remains practical, with cladding and ride height suited to varied road conditions and daily use. This 2018 Subaru Outback 2.5i Limited Crossover combines the 2.5-liter powertrain, all-wheel drive, leather seating, premium audio, smartphone integration, a sunroof, and a hands-free liftgate in one package, and each of those items is visible in the vehicle's equipment rather than in any added description.

With its capable drivetrain, thoughtful features, and Subaru's proven reputation for long-term durability, this Outback presents a compelling option for drivers throughout San Bernardino County who want versatility without sacrificing everyday comfort.About This 2024 Subaru Outback PremiumThis 2024 Subaru Outback Premium comes in a clean white exterior and is equipped with Subaru's signature symmetrical all-wheel drive — a genuine asset for Southern California drivers who deal with everything from mountain passes to desert highways. At 105,787 miles, this Outback has seen real-world use, but that's far from the full story. Subaru Outbacks are widely known for their ability to rack up high mileage while remaining mechanically sound, and with proper service history, this generation of Outback is built to go well beyond 200,000 miles. For buyers who want a late-model vehicle with modern safety and tech features without the premium of a nearly-new price tag, this is exactly the kind of opportunity worth acting on.

The Outback's wagon-style body gives you genuine cargo versatility — more than most crossovers in its class — while keeping a lower ride height that makes loading and unloading practical for daily use.2024 Subaru Outback Performance and EngineUnder the hood sits Subaru's 2.5-liter horizontally opposed four-cylinder engine, a design unique to Subaru that contributes to a lower center of gravity and improved handling balance compared to traditional inline or V-type engines. Power routes through a Lineartronic CVT automatic transmission with an 8-speed manual mode, giving you smooth, seamless acceleration in everyday driving while also allowing you to take more direct control when navigating mountain roads or merging onto the freeway.

Symmetrical AWD is standard across the entire Outback lineup, meaning all four wheels receive power simultaneously rather than only engaging when slip is detected. This proactive approach gives the Outback a confident, planted feel on wet roads, gravel, and uneven terrain — and it's one of the key reasons the Outback has become such a trusted choice for California drivers who split time between urban commutes and weekend adventures in the San Bernardino Mountains or beyond.Subaru Outback Features and InteriorThe Premium trim level sits above the base Outback and adds meaningful upgrades that improve everyday usability. You can expect features such as a larger infotainment display with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto compatibility, heated front seats for cooler desert mornings and mountain evenings, a power moonroof, and upgraded cloth upholstery that holds up well to active lifestyles.

Safety Technology

Every 2024 Subaru Outback comes standard with EyeSight Driver Assist Technology, Subaru's suite of active safety features that includes pre-collision braking, adaptive cruise control, lane-keep assist, and lane departure warning. These are not premium add-ons — they come on every trim, including this Premium, which gives buyers at every price point access to genuinely effective collision-prevention technology that many competing brands still charge extra for.Subaru Outback Reliability and OwnershipThe Subaru Outback consistently ranks among the most reliable midsize crossovers and wagons on the market. J.D. Power, Consumer Reports, and longtime Subaru owners all point to the same conclusion: these vehicles are built to last. The 2.5-liter boxer engine in this generation has a strong track record, and while Subaru owners are advised to stay on top of oil changes and coolant service, there are no widespread mechanical concerns unique to this engine-transmission combination.

The CVT transmission in this generation of Outback is refined and durable when properly maintained — a notable improvement over earlier generations. Owners routinely report 150,000 to 200,000+ miles from these drivetrains with routine maintenance. If you're buying a higher-mileage Subaru, asking for service records and confirming the timing components and fluids are current is always a smart step, and our team at Unique Auto Center is happy to walk you through what we know about this vehicle's history.Why Buy From Unique Auto Center in Bloomington, CaliforniaUnique Auto Center is located in Bloomington, in San Bernardino County, and has built a reputation for offering quality pre-owned vehicles with straightforward, no-pressure service. See our current price on this page and come in for a test drive to experience it for yourself.Financing a Used Subaru Outback Near BloomingtonAt Unique Auto Center, we work with a wide range of lenders to help buyers across the credit spectrum find financing that fits their situation. Whether you have excellent credit, are rebuilding your credit history, or are a first-time buyer, we encourage you to apply — our finance team will work to match you with a loan structure that makes sense for your budget.

This 2024 Subaru Outback is competitively priced for what it offers, and financing through our dealership is a straightforward process. We'll walk you through your options clearly so you can drive away with confidence in both the vehicle and the deal.Frequently Asked Questions

Is the 2024 Subaru Outback a good buy?

Yes — the 2024 Subaru Outback is widely considered one of the best values in the midsize crossover and wagon segment. It combines standard all-wheel drive, advanced safety tech through EyeSight, and a proven powertrain in a practical, comfortable package. For buyers who value reliability and versatility, it consistently earns top recommendations from automotive experts and real-world owners alike.

How many miles is too many on a Subaru Outback?

Subaru Outbacks are well-known for high-mileage longevity. Many owners report 200,000 to 250,000 miles with regular maintenance. A well-maintained Outback at 105,000 miles still has significant life remaining, especially when the service history supports it. The key factors to evaluate are oil change intervals, coolant service, and transmission fluid condition.

What does the Outback Premium trim include?

The Outback Premium trim adds notable upgrades over the base model, including heated front seats, a power moonroof, an 11.6-inch infotainment touchscreen with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, and StarTex water-repellent upholstery in some configurations. All Outbacks — including the Premium — come standard with Subaru EyeSight safety technology and symmetrical AWD.

Is a CVT transmission reliable in the Subaru Outback?

Yes — Subaru's Lineartronic CVT in the current Outback generation has a strong reliability record. When properly maintained (regular fluid changes per Subaru's schedule), it performs smoothly and durably. The 8-speed manual mode also gives drivers a more engaged driving experience when desired.

Does the 2024 Subaru Outback have good safety ratings?

Absolutely. The 2024 Subaru Outback earns top safety marks from both the IIHS and NHTSA.   • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
  • Pedestrian impact prevention - An extra step toward safety. Pedestrians don't always stop, look, and listen, but with Pedestrian Impact Prevention, your vehicle is equipped to better see them and avoid them. This system constantly monitors the road ahead to identify and track pedestrians. It projects that image to an interior display screen, AND should an impact become likely, Pedestrian impact prevention takes steps to avoid a collision.
  • Hands-on cruise control. Set it and forget it. Road trips used to be stressful. Cruise control only managed speed, but not distance or safety. Now, with hands-on cruise control, simply set your desired speed and let sensor technology maintain a safe distance between you and surrounding vehicles. It slows you down, speeds you up and even keeps you in your own lane. Meet your ultimate co-pilot with hands-on cruise control.
  • Rear camera with washer - Watching your back! The rear camera helps you see obstacles and hazards you otherwise couldn't by showing enhanced images of what is behind you. This Gray 2021 Kia Soul GT-Line is the sporty-looking Soul, with 18-inch wheels, fog lights, a sport steering wheel and a power moonroof. Its boxy shape gives you way more headroom and cargo space than you'd expect.

It's smoke-free, had a fresh oil change, and is dealer-inspected. You get Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a backup camera with parking assist, and up to 33 mpg on the highway. It's a great first car, commuter or city car, backed by our Lifetime Powertrain Warranty.

    • Forward collision mitigation - Forward thinking. You look away for just a second and suddenly the vehicle in front of you has stopped. That's when the forward collision mitigation system comes to life. When it senses an impending impact, it will activate a combination of features to help prevent or reduce the severity of an accident. Forward collision mitigation is always looking ahead.
